content.comment_body: I'm experiencing issues with emails on [product_name] [version_no] and firmware [version_no]. The software allows adding email addresses ending with .com, but not those ending with .co.uk. It returns the error 'Removed invalid or duplicate email address'—see attachments for details. Additionally, I'm puzzled as to why login credentials are required for port 25 in legacy usage, since our system normally doesn't require authentication for this port.

It’s unlikely anyone here in the forum can offer a solution. My assumption is that the second dot in addresses like '*.co . uk' might not be permitted. I recommend submitting a formal Support Request for assistance.

I received a response from my support ticket: Thank you for reaching out to [company_name] Technical Support. Regarding your ability to add '.com' but not '.co.uk', this is a recognized issue. Currently, addresses ending with valid multi-part domains like “.co.uk” can't be configured due to syntax limitations. This problem is scheduled to be resolved in a future version of [product_name].
Is this for real from [company_name]? From what I understand, it might require a new hardware revision just to fix this?
I think this will be addressed in the next firmware update ([version_no]).

The reputation for precision is legendary… I also thought the issue was related to [product_name] error itself. By the way, this same bug was present before, in version [version_no] (my previous message in the thread described the same issue).

@[user_name]Support, any updates on an ETA? It's increasingly frustrating that addresses like <phonenumber>@sms.telia.ee still aren't supported and require workarounds, such as sending to a Gmail address and forwarding from there. The last firmware update came out in October 2024.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering restrictions configuring email notifications for certain multi-part domains (such as .co.uk) in [product_name] [version_no] with firmware [version_no], as syntax errors prevent these addresses from being accepted. The issue results in affected addresses being removed as 'invalid or duplicate,' which limits the system’s communication options. There is ongoing user frustration since the problem persists across firmware updates, with no clear timeline for a fix. Users must rely on temporary workarounds and are unsure whether a hardware or firmware solution will resolve the issue.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to send notifications to any valid email address, including those with multi-dot country code domains, and use port 25 for outgoing emails without mandatory login credentials.
